A.span: 任何菩薩若如是已成甚深
A.explanation: The depth applies to the dharma being realized, not to the Bodhisattva.

B.explanation: The text lists aggregates, elements, and sense sources without specifying numbers; standardly there are 18 elements, not 12.
Reverses the meaning by suggesting no merit is obtained, whereas the source asks what merit could be greater than this.

C.explanation: The Tibetan "ཟབ་གྱུར་ཅིང་" means "has become [deep]", modifying the dharma, not the action of "entering" it.
Leaving the conjunction "與" (and) dangling at the end of the line breaks Chinese syntactic rules.
Without punctuation, this naturally reads as "there is no one who realizes this dharma", changing the sentence structure.

A.explanation: The Tibetan "མི་རེག་" means "does not touch" (i.e., does not actualize), rather than "does not seek".

B.explanation: "ལས་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་" means to experience or consume the results of karma, not to "practice" (行持) it.
The text instructs to consider how space itself relies on nothing, rather than viewing space as a vast support.

C.explanation: The Tibetan specifies a chain of dependence (wind on space, water on wind...) and does not mention fire.
Fabricates "beings attain happiness," ignoring the Tibetan which discusses beings experiencing the results of their karma.
The Tibetan instructs to consider what space depends on (nothing), not that space has no intention to abide.

C.span: 習之不住經多歲 射法久習得盡妙 一一箭發無不中
C.explanation: Completely ignores the analogy of shooting successive arrows to keep the first one in the air, replacing it with a description of achieving perfect accuracy.
Omits that this occurs "in a dream" (རྨི་ལམ་ན་), which is a key condition in the source text.
The text says "should be known as prophesied as irreversible," not that he "should be prophesied" or that this is the "irreversible ground".

A.explanation: The commentaries clarify this means "This is taught to be the solitude of the sons of the Sugata," not that the sons of the Sugata are the ones saying it.

C.explanation: Completely omits the key concept of "solitude" or "isolation" (དབེན་པ་), which is the central theme of this stanza.

A.explanation: The term "དྲོད་སྙོམ་" means to measure, judge, or evaluate others (Sanskrit: tulyayati), not "arrogance".

B.explanation: Misinterprets the line. It should mean a bodhisattva who measures/judges others ruins himself, not that having a mind like a scale makes one a bodhisattva.
The Tibetan says "Therefore, one should always engage in wisdom without laziness," not that the merit of Prajna is unconditioned.
The Tibetan does not mention "day and night" (晝夜分).
The Tibetan says Mara becomes "supremely joyful" (མཆོག་ཏུ་ཉམས་བདེར་འགྱུར་), not that he "exerts effort" (精勤).
Omits that this is Mara's thought (སྙམ) and that he thinks "those two" (དེ་གཉིས་) will be far from the Buddha's wisdom.

A.span:
如是行持般若殊勝智者，
說
A.explanation: The text means "It is taught that all perfections of the wise ones are included here," not that the wise ones themselves say this.

C.explanation: Adds 'someone possessing faculties', whereas the Tibetan merely says 'if the life faculty is stopped'.
Omits that all perfections are "subsumed/included" (འདུས་པ་) in wisdom and that this is "taught" (གསུངས).

B.explanation: Mistranslates the negative thought "never think: having realized awakening I will liberate beings" as "preach awakening to the world".
Omits "various births" from the Tibetan text.
Translates "non-conceptualization" (rnam par mi rtog) as "unattached" (無著), which misrepresents the meaning.

A.explanation: Adds "humans" to the text; the Tibetan only specifies "hosts of gods".
Changes the subject. The Tibetan states that the Buddhas express praises, but this translation says the Bodhisattva receives offerings.
Translates "Sons of the Buddhas" (Bodhisattvas) simply as "Buddhas", changing the subject entirely.

B.explanation: Invents "born in Uttarakuru (Northern continent)", completely misunderstanding the analogy.
Translates "having seen those fully possessed objects" as "seeks rebirth there".
Omits the main point of the analogy: that they "do not develop attachment" upon returning.

C.explanation: The punctuation awkwardly splits the noun phrase, impeding readability.
Adds the word "always" (一向), which is not in the source text.
Omits key details of the maidservant analogy: that she is "water-carrying" and "without autonomy".
Entirely omits the fourth line of the Tibetan segment ("Likewise the heroes act under the control of beings").

B.explanation: Reverses the meaning by translating "unskillful bodhisattva" (མི་མཁས་) as "greatly wise bodhisattva".
Misses the specific condition "with the perception of it being long and with suffering", changing it to "long practices asceticism".

B.span: 不離精進波羅蜜 無懈怠心終得證
B.explanation: Reverses the conclusion: the text says they lose diligence and become lazy, but this says they never lose diligence.

C.explanation: Translates "with the perception of suffering" slightly inaccurately as "painfully practice".

A.explanation: Omits "body" (lus), translating simply as the Bodhisattva becoming pure.
Translates "boundless" (pāra) as "paramita/other shore" and completely misses "power/strength".
Completely invents text, replacing the key action "proclaims the supreme Dharma, emptiness" with "hear the dharma and are tamed".
Translates "nges pa" literally as "definitely", missing its context denoting "noble ones" (sūrata).

B.explanation: Misinterprets the subject clause, translating "dharmas that produce bodhi qualities" as "desiring to realize bodhi qualities".
Misses the definitional structure "this is the meaning of morality", translating it instead as "endowed with morality, acts for benefit".

B.span: 若行毀破於尸羅 是則滅壞於菩提
B.explanation: Reverses the logic: the text defines whatever destroys awakening as flawed morality, while the translation states that breaking morality destroys awakening.

C.explanation: Translates "nges pa" literally as "definitely", missing its context denoting "noble ones" (sūrata).
Mistranslates "give away everything", rendering it confusingly as "is called a great wise one for everything".

A.explanation: Omits the chapter title present in the provided Tibetan source.
Adds a line that is not present in the strictly provided Tibetan segment.
